title: Navigating the Official Book by chapter and table
blurb: Know which chapter and table answers which kind of question, recognize which practice a situation belongs to, and know when not to open the book.
question: A question asks which topic of the project kickoff workshop should cover who makes technical decisions. You have three minutes. Which chapter, which section and which table do you open?

teach.body: The Practitioner exam lets you use the PRINCE2 Agile Official Book, with your own notes written inside it, and nothing else. The book only earns marks if you can find a table in seconds. Learn its layout so that a workshop's topics, an artifact's contents or a role's duties are one flick away, and keep your reading time for the scenario and the stems.

teach.h: Look it up, or answer from understanding?

teach.body: In Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares initiation (scenario AS1), the app team and the Coinbridge team argue about who decides on the payment interface design. A question asks which kickoff workshop topic should settle it. You open 13.4 (initiating), find Table 13.8 and scan the topics: icebreaker, psychological safety, values and norms, skill matrix, delegation matrix, team dashboards, project dashboard. The team delegation matrix makes decision authority transparent. Under a minute, one mark.

teach.h: Preparing your book within the rules
items: Write each practice's question (why, who, what if...) beside its x.1 purpose.
Mark every workshop table in chapter 13 and the role table (7.2).
Add cross-references, for example beside Table 12.1: 'checkpoint report = team dashboard'.
Keep all notes inside the book: loose sheets are other material and are not allowed.
Check with PeopleCert or your training provider whether index tabs, highlighting or an eBook are accepted at your sitting.

teach.text: The Agilometer lives in the risk practice (10.3.2), not in progress, quality or a 'focus areas' chapter: Version 1's focus areas are gone. Likewise, the agile versions of reports sit in the progress chapter (Table 12.1): the team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report, the project dashboard replaces the highlight and end stage reports.

items: Practices are chapters 6 to 12; processes and workshops are chapter 13.
In a practice chapter: x.1 purpose, x.3 guidance and artifacts, x.4 techniques.
Roles: Table 7.2 and Appendix B. Fix and flex: Table 3.1. Principles: Table 5.1.
Match the situation to a practice by the question it answers.
Look up facts; decide verdicts from understanding, then confirm one fact.

summary: You can now find any practice, process, workshop or role table in the Official Book quickly, and match a scenario situation to the practice whose purpose it serves. You also know which questions to answer from understanding rather than by searching.

A.q: During Fair Fares initiation at Larkspur Rail, the project manager sets out how procurement and the Coinbridge contract will support agile delivery, including a fixed team cost per iteration and an agreed Definition of Done. Which practice is being applied?
A.why: The commercial management approach, which should support agile product development, belongs to the organization practice (7.3.2).

whyNot.0: The business case covers justification; contract arrangements sit in the commercial management approach.
whyNot.1: The Definition of Done is a quality artifact, but setting up the contract is an organization concern.
whyNot.3: Issues handles changes to the baseline; no change is being assessed here.

A.q: At the end of Stage 2 of Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares project, the government announces higher penalties for late compensation. The board asks for the project canvas to be updated so it can judge whether the project is still worth the investment. Which practice is being applied?
A.why: The business case practice judges whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable; the project canvas is its agile form (6.1, 6.3.2).

whyNot.1: Progress compares actual against planned; the board here is checking justification.
whyNot.2: Risk handles uncertainties; the penalty change has already happened.
whyNot.3: Plans defines products and the means to deliver them, not whether the project is worthwhile.

A.q: A Practitioner question about Larkspur Rail's app team asks which topic of the team retrospective workshop should cover the team's suggestions for improving its testing. Where in the Official Book should the candidate look?
options: Section 13.5, the controlling a stage process
A.why: The team retrospective workshop supports managing product delivery (13.6.4.2, Table 13.14).

whyNot.0: Controlling a stage hosts the progress review workshop, not the team retrospective.
whyNot.1: The quality chapter covers testing techniques, not the retrospective's agenda.
whyNot.2: The progress chapter covers dashboards and reports, not workshop agendas.

B.q: During Stage 3 of Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares project, a tester finds that the completed matching model wrongly rejects one valid ticket type, so it will not meet its agreed acceptance criteria. Which practice handles this situation?
B.why: A product that will not meet its quality specification is an off-specification, one of the issue types defined in 11.3.1 and handled by the issues practice.

whyNot.0: Quality sets the requirements and the means to meet them; a product already failing them is an off-specification issue.
whyNot.2: Risk covers uncertain events; this has already happened.
whyNot.3: Progress compares actual with planned; the deviation itself is captured as an issue.

B.q: Larkspur Rail's finance director wants a ten-page monthly written report. The project manager proposes a project dashboard that the board can check at any time instead. A candidate wants to confirm which traditional report the project dashboard replaces. Where should she look?
B.why: The progress practice's artifacts table (Table 12.1) maps the highlight and end stage reports to the project dashboard.

whyNot.0: Table 8.1 covers plans artifacts such as the release map.
whyNot.2: The progress review workshop reviews the dashboard, but the mapping of reports to artifacts is in Table 12.1.
whyNot.3: Table 3.1 sets fix and flex defaults for the performance aspects.

B.q: In Fair Fares initiation, Larkspur Rail's project manager wants every participant to rate how well the environment suits agile working, including how far the Coinbridge contract allows flexibility and how easily the teams communicate. Which practice does this tool belong to?
B.why: The Agilometer identifies and monitors the risks of agile working and sits in the risk practice (10.3.2).

whyNot.0: Dashboards may show Agilometer trends, but the tool is a risk management product.
whyNot.1: Quality covers requirements and acceptance, not the risks of agile working.
whyNot.2: Contracts are organization topics, but rating the environment for agile is the Agilometer, a risk tool.

C.q: Facing an 'Is this an appropriate application of the business case practice, and why?' item about Larkspur Rail, Sam reads the whole of chapter 6 before deciding on a verdict, taking seven minutes. Is this an appropriate use of the book, and why?
options: Yes, because reasons in these items quote the book closely
Yes, because business case items need the full chapter
No, because the verdict comes from understanding first
No, because the business case chapter is not examined
C.why: Verdicts come from reading the situation against the method; the book is used to settle one fact, within about three minutes per question.

whyNot.0: Even where a reason echoes the book, reading a whole chapter spends over twice the three minutes a question allows.
whyNot.1: A judgement item turns on understanding, not on rereading a chapter.
whyNot.3: The business case practice is examined in the practices section.

C.q: Fair Fares is a contractual requirement for Larkspur Rail, which faces penalties from January. During starting up, the project manager suggests that no business case is needed because the contract makes the project compulsory. Is this an appropriate application of the business case practice, and why?
options: Yes, because a contractual duty provides the justification
Yes, because the project canvas replaces the business case
No, because even compulsory projects need a justification
No, because the CPO owns the business case for the project
C.why: All projects need business justification; in PRINCE2 Agile the business case is tailored, for example as a project canvas, not dropped (5.2.1.1, 6.3.2).

whyNot.0: Compulsory work still needs its chosen option justified.
whyNot.1: The project canvas is a tailored business case, not a reason to have none.
whyNot.3: The project executive is accountable for the business case, not the CPO.

C.q: Larkspur Rail's project manager asks the app team's product owner for a weekly written checkpoint report. The team coach suggests instead that the team keeps a team dashboard which the project manager can check at any time. Is the team coach's suggestion an appropriate application of the progress practice, and why?
options: Yes, because the team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report
Yes, because the board reviews team dashboards at progress reviews
No, because checkpoint reports are a required PRINCE2 product
No, because dashboards replace highlight reports, not checkpoints
C.why: In PRINCE2 Agile the team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report, and the project manager pulls information from it (Table 12.1).

whyNot.1: Progress reviews look at the project dashboard; team dashboards are reviewed in team workshops.
whyNot.2: Management products are tailored in PRINCE2 Agile; the team dashboard is the agile form.
whyNot.3: The project dashboard replaces the highlight report; the team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report.

reteach.title: Use the book like a supermarket map
reteach.question: In a supermarket you know roughly where the bread is. How does that help in the exam?

blocks.body: You do not read every shelf label; you know dairy is at the back. Learn the book the same way: practices in aisles 6 to 12, processes and workshops in 13, roles in Table 7.2, fix and flex in Table 3.1. Then each look-up is a short walk.

items: Decide what kind of fact you need.
Go straight to its chapter and table.
If it is a judgement, answer before you open the book.

explain.h: Plans: what, how, when, how much
explain.body: The plans practice defines the products to deliver and the means: who, how and where, with estimates of when and how much.

test.q: In Fair Fares initiation, Larkspur Rail's project manager clusters user stories into three releases and estimates when each release can go live. Which practice is being applied?
test.why: Defining which products are delivered when, through the release map, is the plans practice (8.1, 8.3.2).

whyNot.0: Progress tracks actual against the plan once work is under way.
whyNot.1: The business case judges whether the project is worthwhile.
whyNot.3: Quality covers users' requirements and acceptance, not release scheduling.

explain.body: The quality practice documents users' requirements of the products and how they will be met, for example through acceptance criteria and the Definition of Done.

test.q: About 12% of Larkspur Rail's passengers have a disability or long-term condition. The CPO asks that every Fair Fares story carry acceptance criteria showing the app meets accessibility standards. Which practice is being applied?
test.why: Defining what users will accept and how it is measured is the quality practice (9.1).

whyNot.0: Risk covers uncertainties, not acceptance criteria.
whyNot.2: Plans schedules the work; the criteria themselves are a quality concern.
whyNot.3: Issues handles changes and problems once they arise.

explain.body: Starting up is 13.2, directing 13.3, initiating 13.4, controlling a stage 13.5, managing product delivery 13.6, managing a stage boundary 13.7 and closing 13.8.

test.q: A question asks which topic of Larkspur Rail's project initiation workshop should agree the project-wide criteria an epic must meet before work starts. Which section should the candidate open?
test.why: The project initiation workshop supports initiating a project (13.4.4.1, Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: Starting up hosts the project canvas and starting up workshops.
whyNot.1: Directing hosts the agile enablement workshop.
whyNot.2: The stage boundary hosts the release planning workshop.

explain.body: The 11 PRINCE2 Agile roles and their responsibilities are in the organization chapter (Table 7.2), with full role descriptions in Appendix B (Table B.1).

test.q: A Larkspur Rail question asks whether the team coach should help the app team write user stories. The candidate wants to confirm the team coach's responsibilities. Which table should she open?
test.why: Role responsibilities are in Table 7.2, with full descriptions in Appendix B.

whyNot.1: Table 13.8 lists the kickoff workshop's topics, not role duties.
whyNot.3: Table 5.2 summarizes how the practices apply in agile.
